alternatives_and_negative_results: Do not normalize or clip input to force fit, and do not use a single gain profile to imply coverage of all source classes.
applicability: Fixed-point radar processing where input dynamic range and source profiles are controlled.
assessed_root_cause: Gain scaling and quantization define the numeric input presented to the fixed-point chain; clipping changes the experiment and must remain visible.
author_role: historical project engineering record, backfilled by FPGA engineering copilot
chosen_corrective_method: Preserve source Float, raw integer IQ, Q1.15 bytes, metadata and hashes; validate envelope, signed fit, clip count and conservative headroom before processing.
generalizable_lesson: Input quantization is part of the system contract and its admission decision, not a preprocessing convenience.
initial_faulty_assumption_or_design_deci: Input conversion could be treated as a harmless serialization detail or clipping could be hidden by saturation and still counted as normal performance.
non_applicability: Does not establish headroom for the untested SCR +/-10 dB clutter envelope or other target/clutter mixtures.
observable_consequence: C01/C02 specify ties-to-even conversion, signed Q1.15 IQ, profile-specific gain and clipping reporting; all 16 C06R2 inputs passed no-clipping and static headroom preflight.
observed_problem: The same normalized source is represented at different approved gains; conversion and clipping affect every downstream fixed-point stage.
repeatable_validation: Check C01 signoff, selected-C input mapping and C06R2 manifest for 16/16 ready, zero clipped components and headroom PASS.
reviewer_role: documentary evidence validation by FPGA engineering copilot; not a separate human reviewer
safety_contract_constraints: No change to C01 profile gains, Q1.15 mapping, RNE, clipping policy or prelocked C06R2 data.
title: Treat input gain, Q1.15 conversion and clipping as explicit admission controls
